- When sentiment turns negative in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior day) and sentiment is neutral or negative, cap the forecast at 1–2 days above the prior peak to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true price by >5% over 3–5 days, apply a “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–2% per day from forecast if sentiment is mixed or negative.  
- When sentiment is uniformly positive for 5+ days, allow a 3–5% upward bias, but cap at 10% above recent 7-day average to avoid over-leveraging.  
- If true price drops sharply after a forecast peak (e.g., >10% drop in 3 days), assume sentiment shift and adjust next forecast downward by 5–8% to reflect “reversal bias.”  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment history shows 3+ negative signals in last 7 days, reduce forecast by 3–5% to reflect “sentiment drag.”
